observations.statement: The core maps terminal rerun, restart_replace, show, and split_pane from the shared Terminal and bottom runtime panels to four distinct UICommand identifiers and four distinct terminal handlers; all four declare no expected persisted event type.

Each terminal entry requires typed dispatcher registration, a projected availability selector and disabled reason, dispatch evidence carrying command and correlation metadata plus result/effect, a no-persist disposition, and regression evidence before production certification.
Terminal rerun binds availability and disabled copy to named state projections, requires a no-persist dispatch receipt or route/open disposition, and forbids unexpected persisted domain events.

Terminal rerun explicitly requires stable role/name/description semantics, keyboard reachability and activation, visible focus with deterministic post-dispatch-or-error return, and assistive announcement of its disabled reason.

The testing capability policy command is routed to handlers::testing::capability_policy_set, emits testing.capability_policy.updated, persists Auto/On/Off at global/project scope, appears in an effective policy snapshot, enumerates disabled-reason categories, and prohibits silent enablement when test capability is unavailable.

Capability-policy production certification requires typed Automated Testing owner evidence, named state and disabled-reason projections, event/correlation evidence, accessibility evidence, and a regression oracle; its event test asserts the event type and four dispatch identity fields.

The testing-session background command is routed to handlers::testing::session_background and emits testing.session.backgrounded while preserving visible session identity, receipt references, a recovery route, and evidence streams; it must neither mark testing complete nor hide critical blockers.

Session backgrounding enumerates no-active-session, required-attention, redaction-block, and policy-forced-foreground disabled reasons, binds named state projections, and requires matching assistive disabled announcement plus deterministic focus handling.
The background event contract requires dispatch-correlation evidence, and its event test asserts testing.session.backgrounded plus command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.

candidate_findings.title: Terminal actions lack command-specific behavior contracts
candidate_findings.statement: The four terminal records identify action names and handler targets, but their acceptance blocks only define common dispatch, projection, receipt, accessibility, and evidence scaffolding. No core clause defines which terminal, pane, process, command, or session is targeted or the observable postcondition of rerun, restart_replace, show, or split_pane.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent builders can implement materially different target selection and user-visible outcomes while satisfying every listed wiring check, so the four capabilities are not behaviorally deterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Required typed command contracts are not specified
candidate_findings.statement: Every command requires typed args/result or a typed payload/result contract, but the assigned core supplies no input fields, output fields, value types, validation constraints, or error variants for any of the six commands.
candidate_findings.impact: Dispatcher, handler, UI, fixture, and event producers can adopt incompatible contracts, and the demanded typed-contract certification has no exact schema oracle.

candidate_findings.title: No-persist receipt and disposition semantics are underdefined
candidate_findings.statement: The terminal contracts permit a no-persist command receipt or a route/open disposition and name a rerun receipt reference, but they do not select the valid alternative per action or define receipt/disposition fields, success and failure states, recording time, retention, or durability.
candidate_findings.impact: Incomparable or transient artifacts could satisfy the text without proving whether dispatch ran, failed, or produced the intended terminal effect.

candidate_findings.title: Terminal availability and disabled-reason rules have no domain conditions
candidate_findings.statement: All four terminal entries require projected availability and a disabled reason, but no command-specific unavailable states, safety predicates, reason codes, reason precedence, or projection freshness rule appears in their core contracts.
candidate_findings.impact: Unsafe or impossible terminal actions may remain enabled, and different implementations can surface contradictory disabled truth while using the required projection plumbing.

candidate_findings.title: Accessibility acceptance leaves consequential values open
candidate_findings.statement: The accessibility clauses require a stable role/name/description matching each command and deterministic focus return, but do not state the actual semantic role, accessible name or description, the focus destination, or visibility rule that activates keyboard obligations.
candidate_findings.impact: Different controls can pass qualitative checks while presenting inconsistent semantics or returning focus to different locations, weakening repeatable accessibility certification.

candidate_findings.title: Effective testing-policy resolution is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The policy setter must persist Auto/On/Off at global/project scope and display inherited/effective policy, but the core does not define Auto semantics, global-versus-project precedence, inheritance and override rules, missing-scope behavior, or how concurrent/stale project context affects resolution.
candidate_findings.impact: The same stored policy inputs can yield different effective capability and approval behavior, including erroneous enablement or disablement across projects.

candidate_findings.title: Policy event evidence does not prove the policy change
candidate_findings.statement: The policy requirement concerns selected mode, persistence scope, and the effective snapshot, while the declared event test asserts only the event type plus command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target; it does not require selected mode, scope, previous value, stored value, effective value, or inheritance source.
candidate_findings.impact: An implementation can emit a correctly correlated testing.capability_policy.updated event while persisting or projecting the wrong policy and still satisfy the stated event oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Background transition and recovery behavior are not defined
candidate_findings.statement: The background action names preservation and safety invariants but does not define foreground/background states, transition ordering or atomicity, the identity and freshness rules for the visible session, what constitutes an evidence stream or critical blocker, the recovery-route target, or behavior if the session completes or fails concurrently.
candidate_findings.impact: Backgrounding can lose recovery continuity, expose stale session truth, or hide completion and blocker changes despite superficially retaining references.

candidate_findings.title: Background event evidence omits domain postconditions
candidate_findings.statement: The background event test asserts only testing.session.backgrounded and dispatch identity metadata; it does not require the session identity, receipt references, recovery route, preserved evidence streams, resulting background state, completion state, or blocker visibility named by the acceptance checks.
candidate_findings.impact: A correlated event can pass certification even when the user loses the session, its evidence, its recovery path, or visibility of critical blockers.

candidate_findings.title: Lifecycle, duplicate-dispatch, concurrency, and failure semantics are absent
candidate_findings.statement: Across the six command entries, the common contracts require a result and evidence but do not define cancellation, retry, idempotency, duplicate dispatch, concurrent invocation, partial failure, timeout, or rollback behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Reruns or replacements can duplicate or race terminal processes, policy writes can overwrite newer state, and background transitions can conflict with session completion without a normative resolution.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Command identifiers, handler targets, shared UI locations, and empty expected persisted-event sets are explicit for all four terminal controls.
For terminal rerun, the core explicitly requires a no-persist receipt or disposition and explicitly rejects any unexpected persisted domain event.
Terminal rerun has explicit availability and disabled-reason projection paths and explicit keyboard, focus, semantic, and disabled-announcement obligations.
The policy command explicitly names its three policy modes, persistence scopes, effective-snapshot visibility, five disabled-reason categories, and the no-silent-enablement regression invariant.
The policy command's handler, expected event type, Automated Testing evidence owner, state projections, and dispatch-correlation evidence obligation are explicit.
Session backgrounding explicitly preserves session identity, receipt references, recovery routing, and evidence streams and explicitly forbids marking testing complete or hiding critical blockers.

The background command's handler, expected event type, four disabled-reason categories, state projections, Automated Testing evidence owner, accessibility obligations, and event-correlation test are explicit.

unknowns.statement: The exact input, output, validation, and failure types for all six commands are unknown within the assigned core.
The target-selection and observable state-change semantics of rerun, restart_replace, show, and split_pane are unknown.
The schema, retention, durability, and success/failure lifecycle of terminal dispatch receipts and route/open dispositions are unknown.
The terminal conditions that make each command unavailable and the precedence and representation of its disabled reasons are unknown.
The resolution algorithm for Auto, global and project scope, inheritance, overrides, and stale project context is unknown.
The domain payload and atomic persistence-to-event relationship for testing.capability_policy.updated are unknown.
The formal background state transition, recovery route contract, session freshness rule, and definitions of required attention and critical blockers are unknown.
The domain payload and atomic state-to-event relationship for testing.session.backgrounded are unknown.
Cancellation, retry, idempotency, duplicate-dispatch, concurrency, timeout, partial-failure, and rollback behavior are unknown for all six commands.
The actual accessible roles, names, descriptions, keyboard visibility condition, and post-dispatch or error focus targets are unknown.
